title: Prescribed moving harmonic holonomy costs total variation rather than connection amplitude

moving_holonomy.equation: For C1 a(t) on the torus, solve phi_tt+L_(a(t))phi=0 with L_a=-(grad-i e a)^2+m^2 and m>0.
moving_holonomy.exact_derivative: For H_a=(1/2)(||phi_t||^2+<phi,L_a phi>), H_a'=-(e dot a) dot sum_k (k-ea)|phi_k|^2.
moving_holonomy.relative_bound: The scalar inequality 2m|p|<=|p|^2+m^2 gives |H_a'|<=(|e|/m)|dot a|H_a and H_a(t)<=H_a(0)exp((|e|/m)TV(a)).
moving_holonomy.charge_hierarchy: The global charge generator commutes with L_(a(t)) for every t, so the same bound holds at every charge tier and for positive analytic sums.
moving_holonomy.maxwell_interpretation: In temporal gauge dot a=-mean(E); the cost is harmonic electric variation, while static generic flat holonomy has zero cost without requiring periodic gauge removal.
moving_holonomy.scope_guard: The identity treats prescribed harmonic a(t) and positive mass. It does not prove coupled Maxwell-current control, finite total variation, radial control or global continuation.
